idiom_name: records/POJOs + MapStruct or hand-written assembler + repository interface
implementation_notes: The mainstream separated form on the JVM is a domain layer of POJOs or records with factory methods and no Jakarta imports, plus an infrastructure layer that holds JPA entities (annotated, storage-shaped) and an assembler that converts between them - hand-written or generated by MapStruct; a domain-owned repository interface is implemented with Spring Data or plain JDBC, and the mapper replaces the entity graph the ORM would otherwise build. Annotating the domain classes directly is the trap this pattern exists to avoid: JPA needs no-arg constructors, non-final classes, mutable fields and lazy proxies, all of which push the model towards an anemic, context-bound entity.
pitfalls: Two models plus mapping code is real cost: without MapStruct or discipline, entity and domain drift apart and a field is forgotten in one direction only.
JPA repository methods leak entities (and IQueryable-like Specifications) into the application; returning entities from an interface that claims to speak domain types is the most common erosion.
MapStruct generates code silently - unmapped target properties are warnings unless unmappedTargetPolicy is escalated, so renamed columns can vanish without failing the build.

variants.name: JPA with externalized (XML) mapping over clean domain classes
variants.idiom_name: JPA/Hibernate with orm.xml mapping, no annotations on the model
variants.implementation_notes: The persistence provider itself becomes the mapper: Hibernate maps the domain classes from externalized metadata (orm.xml) instead of annotations, so the model stays annotation-free while change tracking and lazy loading remain available. This is the oldest JVM answer to persistence ignorance and still the only way to keep Hibernate's full object-graph mapping without touching the classes; it costs XML that must be maintained alongside the model, which is why most teams prefer the explicit mapper variant unless they need the ORM's identity map and cascades on the domain objects themselves.
variants.code_sketch:
<!-- META-INF/orm.xml - mapping lives outside the classes -->
<entity class="com.acme.domain.Order" access="FIELD">
  <table name="orders"/>
  <attributes>
    <id name="id"/>
    <basic name="total"><column name="total_cents"/></basic>
  </attributes>
</entity>
// domain.Order has no @Entity, @Id or @Column anywhere
pitfalls: JPA rules still apply to the class shape (no-arg constructor, non-final class, mutable or field-accessible state) - XML removes the annotations, not the requirements.
Detached entities and lazy loading: if a mapped domain object escapes the persistence context, navigating an unloaded relation throws LazyInitializationException.
orm.xml drifts silently from the code: a renamed property that is not updated breaks at startup or, worse, maps the wrong column.
